title: Recovery, therapy and deciding to live together
summary: After surgery at the hands of a DeBakey student, Virginia nursed him back to health in Leisuretown with therapy in Lawrenceville, and they decided to share their life; he moved in about 1972.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yes. He first tried to transfer arteries to save his leg and it wasn't successful. There was a long series of just terrible, absolutley terrible. And we came through that. And then well our romance had just taken place. And I said, who is going to take care of Chauncey. Because he was living in his home at that time.

Right here. I had come here to be near my children. And for a while, Susan, she was crying. What am I going to do with my daddy. And you know, both had three stories to contend with. I said bring him here. I said bring him around here because he was out of it. He just had it. So anyhow I nursed him back to health. That's it.
And we went to therapy which was three times a week to Lawrenceville, that's just this side of Princeton. And we had to learn how to use weights and exercise things.
all kinds of things. And he recovered from it so marvelously. Of course being in love does an awful lot to make a person get well.
Because the doctors never heard of it because this guy here, he could get up from the floor with one leg which they said for a man his age was practically impossible.
Chauncey could now have strength in his arms.
And he used to do exercises with these - what do you call these?
Indian clubs and he worked out on those. And he just could do everything. I mean tricks like match slinging and things. Anyhow that's how that grew. And so we decided to spend our life together.
Uh huh. What year was it that he moved in this house?
In this house, '74. I don't know.
Oh, it was eight years ago. 1972, I'm sorry. I was wrong, '72. It was eight years.
